text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 12 in history.
1492 - Christopher Columbus made his first landfall in the New World. His crew landed in the Bahamas after a 33-day voyage from the Canary Islands, initially believing they had found Asia.
1576 - Maximilian II, Holy Roman emperor since 1564, died. He was succeeded by his brother Rudolf II.

1810 - Bavarian Crown Prince Ludwig married Princess Therese of Saxony-Hildburghausen. The festivities became an annual event and evolved into the present-day Oktoberfest celebration of beer and bratwurst.
1811 - Paraguay declared its independence from Spain and Argentina.
1822 - Brazil formally became independent of Portugal.
1870 - Robert E(dward) Lee, commander of the Southern armies during the American civil war, died.
1928 - The first "iron lung" was used at Boston Children's Hospital, Massachusetts.

1935 - Luciano Pavarotti, internationally popular Italian opera singer, born. Famous for Verdi arias such as "La donna e mobile" from "Rigoletto" along with popular Italian songs such as "O Sole Mio".
1960 - Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev, angered during a debate on colonialism at the U.N. General Assembly, took off his shoe and pounded his desk with it several times.
1967 - 66 people were killed when a BEA Comet airliner crashed in the Mediterranean.
1968 - Equatorial Guinea became independent after 190 years of Spanish rule, its first president being Francisco Macias Nguema.
1971 - Dean Acheson, U.S. politician and secretary of state from 1949 to 1953, died.
1973 - Juan Peron was inaugurated as Argentine president, with his wife, Isabel, as vice-president.
1976 - Chinese Prime Minister Hua Guofeng was appointed Chairman of the Communist Party.
1978 - Egyptian-Israeli peace treaty negotiations were opened in Washington by U.S. President Jimmy Carter.
1983 - Former Japanese prime minister Kakuei Tanaka was sentenced to four years' imprisonment for his part in the Lockheed bribery scandal.
1984 - Five people were killed when an Irish Republican Army (IRA) bomb exploded at the Grand Hotel in Brighton, England, during the annual Conservative Party conference.
1986 - A summit conference between U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev ended in Reykjavik without reaching any agreement on arms control.

1989 - Former Argentine military leader Leopoldo Galtieri and two other members of the junta who led the country into the Falklands War against Britain, were released from jail after receiving presidential pardons.
1989 - Christer Pettersson, sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of Swedish prime minister Olof Palme, was freed by the Court of Appeal.
1990 - Motorcycle gunmen killed Egyptian parliamentary speaker Rifaat Mahjoub and three of his bodyguards in a machinegun ambush in Cairo.

1992 - More than 550 people were killed and almost 10,000 injured when an earthquake, measuring 5.9 on the Richter scale, struck Cairo. The epicentre was not far from the great pyramids of Giza and the Sphinx.

1994 - President Boris Yeltsin fired acting Finance Minister Sergei Dubinin and demanded the head of conservative Central Bank chief Viktor Gerashchenko as the hunt for a scapegoat for Russia's rouble collapse began.
